correctness.rationale: In the inclusive ordered nerve, only degrees 0–2 have nondegenerate cells. Backtrack triangles identify reverse unit edges as inverses; choosing a path to replace each distance-two edge leaves exactly triangle and square relations on graph paths. A square with a chord already contracts by triangles. In a Hamming graph, coordinate squares commute consecutive changes in different coordinates, leaving closed walks in complete factors, which contract by triangles or backtracks. Thus X is simply connected including q=2. The cell counts n, n(s+t), ns² give χ(X)=nk; integral H_2 is free as a subgroup of C_2, and Hurewicz and homological Whitehead give the wedge of nk−1 spheres. A translation fixing a point would preserve its unique nondegenerate simplex and hence fix its ordered first vertex. The free finite action is a covering with deck group T, so the quotient has π_1 and H_1 equal to T, χ=k and torsion-free H_2 of rank k−1. The equivariant Euler characteristic over Q is k regular characters, since each orbit of cells is a copy of T without a sign twist. Subtracting the trivial degree-zero character gives the claimed representation by semisimplicity. Nothing requires q prime. An independent exact H(2,3) computation gave cover counts (9,72,144), ranks (8,64), and quotient counts (1,8,16) with Smith factors 1^6,3², consistent with β_2=80 and quotient rank 8. value.rationale: Length two is the first scale permitting two-dimensional attaching maps, and Hamming products and their regular translations give a natural test family beyond triangle-free graphs and the binary cube. The ordered construction produces a uniform exact homotopy type, explicit torsion in the canonical quotient, and a complete rational translation character, all useful invariants not supplied by the corresponding Rips calculations. It is the concrete computation for this model, not the textbook covering, Euler characteristic or semisimplicity deductions in isolation, that carries value.
